<a id="giving-that-waits-on-giving"></a>
### Giving that waits on giving

- **Mechanism.** Each formation gives at a step according to whether what it waits on gave; the relation of waiting is given, with no finiteness and no decision of equality or of giving. With memory (waitsAll: gives where it gave and everything it waits on gave), a formation gives at step n exactly where every formation within n waits of it gave at the start, so a withholding stays and spreads downstream along every chain of waits; one withholding, where every formation lies within d waits of it, ends all giving from step d on. Without memory (answers: gives where what it waits on gave at the step before), a formation gives at n exactly where every formation with a chain of exactly n waits to it gave at the start; where no chain of L waits exists every formation gives from L on, whatever the start, and on a loop of p waits a withholding returns at every multiple of p. Under both laws more waiting gives no more at any step: whatever gives under the added waits gives without them. In a ring of three (a witness), from one withholding, with memory all withhold from step 2, without memory the withholding circulates.

<a id="restoring-giving-from-the-worst-start"></a>
### Restoring giving from total withholding

- **Mechanism.** For every law of giving that keeps inclusion (more giving at a step gives no less at the next), a formation gives at step n from every start exactly where it gives at n from total withholding, and from that start giving only grows, so restoring by n is restoring at every later step; where no formation gives at the step after total withholding, none gives at any step of the course from it. Under giving first, a source giving whatever it waits on and the others answering, call a chain of waits clear where none of its formations after the first is a source; with the sources decided, a formation gives at n from every start exactly where no clear chain of n waits leads into it, and a clear loop is never restored. Without memory the same holds of every chain, so, with the sources decided, giving first never restores later than waiting on all; with memory no step restores giving. The ring of three has no clear chain of three waits, so its restoring from step 3 is an instance.

<a id="thresholds-of-waiting"></a>
### Thresholds of waiting

- **Mechanism.** Under the tolerating law a formation gives where all but its tolerance of what it waits on gave, what it waits on a given list and its tolerance a given number; with every tolerance zero it is answers on the listed waits. A set giving at the start, each member waiting on at most its tolerance outside it, keeps giving whatever the rest does; a thin withholding, every formation waiting on at most its tolerance inside it and the start giving outside it, passes out in one step. Restoring needs a formation that spares all it waits on, which gives at every step after the start whatever the start: from total withholding a giving formation finds one, and where no formation spares all it waits on, total withholding, once reached, stays. In a triad one withholding spreads to all with tolerance zero and passes out with tolerance one, while with tolerance one total withholding is kept (a witness). For the same waits and start, a formation giving under a tolerating law gives under every tolerating law with tolerances no smaller, at every step. On a web where each formation depends only on its own condition, at a need k no more than the number upstream, and that condition receives one unit from each upstream formation supported the step before, support is a run of the tolerating law with tolerance the number upstream less k (the web reading, on the World).
- **Base.** any type
- **How far seen.** [thresholds-of-waiting](../../records/thresholds-of-waiting.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [tolerance-monotone-across-laws](../../records/tolerance-monotone-across-laws.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="a-pair-tolerates-only-within-a-window"></a>
### A pair tolerates only within a window

- **Mechanism.** Two formations each waiting on the other, giving decided for the one-step laws; for the windowed law any type and any relation of waiting, errors a supplied pattern that only turn a giving into withholding. In a pair a tolerance of one is giving whatever comes, so a pair passes a withholding out only through time. Under answers one withholding after mutual giving echoes: at every step exactly one of the pair gives, and they never give together again, the return of a withholding on a loop of two waits. Of the eight one-step laws giving after mutual giving, five keep inclusion, and each either never restores mutual giving after one withholding or never answers a constant withholder. Answering within a window of w gives where each formation waited on gave at one of its last w steps, on the whole history; a wider window gives no less, and where every formation waits on some formation no window restores from total withholding. No window both absorbs one error and answers within an error pattern in which no formation errs at two consecutive steps; the alternator is its instance, its partner giving at every step under every window of at least two.

<a id="errors-by-chance-in-a-pair-keeping-mutual-withholding"></a>
### Errors by chance in a pair keeping mutual withholding

- **Mechanism.** A pair's run of two laws of giving; errors only withhold, read from a course of values, each formation's error at a step weighing p and its step without one q, in natural numbers; near-definitional once errors are one-way and a law keeps mutual withholding. A law keeps mutual withholding where, after two steps at which both formations withheld, it withholds: answering, the window of two, waiting on both and withholding do; agreement, sparing and the alternator do not. Where both formations err at two consecutive steps, a pair of such laws withholds at every step from the first of them on, whatever the errors after. Of the courses of 4k values, whose whole weight is ((p + q)^4)^k, those under which a formation still gives at step 2k weigh at most ((p + q)^4 - p^4)^k, and where an error weighs something the block's part is less than the whole. A witness: for a pair of windows of two, each value weighing one, twelve of the sixteen courses of four values still give at step two, against the bound fifteen. A step at which neither gives need not be total withholding. By hand, not in the Lean: where an error has a positive chance such a pair ends in total withholding with probability one.

<a id="offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits"></a>
### Offspring read from giving that waits

- **Mechanism.** Over n steps of a pair's run each formation has two counts, the steps its partner gave it and the steps it withheld, theorems of the runs for every n. Its offspring are read, while it is supported, as a + β·received + γ·withheld, with natural factors, a supplied reading: the formula, the pairing and the formation's being supported over the run are premises, not shown of any actual case, and cohorts are read one at a time, no law here being of a course of cohorts. Pairs read as groups of two of the multilevel law. Where β ≤ γ, in every cohort listed as pairs whose places not of a kind withhold, the kind does not rise, whatever laws it holds and whatever the errors; member by member this fails with errors, since an answerer erring at every step beside an answerer leaves β more than a withholder beside a withholder (a witness). In mixed pairs with alternators the window of two never rises, for any β and γ. Where every law gives after mutual giving and none errs, every place leaves the same and nothing is selected. Which sign holds is not derived here.
- **Base.** a named model

<a id="what-decides-giving-against-keeping-on-a-flow"></a>
### What decides giving against keeping on a flow

- **Mechanism.** A pair's run as a balanced flow, the parts supplied, offspring read as the level of a line; near-definitional once the parts are fixed. Two balanced flows from the same levels whose takes and gives on each condition, at each step at which the levels agree, differ only by amounts that cancel keep the same levels. With routes (standings constant, the parts the same for both, so renewal reaching one only is not represented) a place's offspring is the pair formula for any laws and errors. With renewal while standing (given only while its formation is active), from the same standings, the same renewal and draws, one gift amount arriving whole and each need covering upkeep, the line's part and the gift, mutual giving at every step leaves the levels as no giving does while both stand; one-sided giving is not covered, and changes the standings. Under that renewal a formation below its need, its partner giving it nothing, never stands again. At a shortfall, in single witnesses, a line gaining its part exactly at the steps its formation stands, by construction: from standings at their needs a formation giving to one that never gives falls below its need and never stands again, its line over m + 1 steps m short of what keeping leaves it, while the receiver, standing in both runs, leaves the same, although what it holds at step 1 differs; in a pair that keeps, one draw of two from a standing at its need ends the renewal for good.

<a id="what-giving-that-waits-draws-on"></a>
### What giving that waits draws on

- **Mechanism.** Single small witnesses on balanced webs, not general laws of renewal or need, show two ways a gift can bring support beyond what it draws on the giver. Need asymmetry within the pair: in a balanced pair into which nothing flows, a giver at level two moving one unit to a receiver at level one leaves both supported where the needs are one and two, and only moves support where they are two and two, the giver unsupported at every later step and leaving no descendant. Renewal from outside: a renewer whose giving does not require its own level lets the giver give one unit at every step without its level falling, the gifts over any N steps totalling N, the inflow into the pair. Read a factor of the offspring as a line's rise per step on a balanced web with no dependence beyond broken (a supplied reading): β times the received count is at most the slack beyond and the inflow summed over those steps, and γ likewise. Both bounds have one form, so neither compares β with γ.

<a id="a-circular-wait-needs-a-reserve-present"></a>
### A circular dependence: maintenance running or a wait no one can begin

- **Mechanism.** A witness on Boolean configurations, one step at a time, in a periphery module (propext in some of the cited declarations and none in the others, as its receipt reports; Quot.sound enters only absent_reserve_blocks_ignition). In a shared renewal whose two sides each pass their activity to the other at every step, joint activity at any step is exactly joint activity at the start: an empty start stays empty, and a one-sided start never becomes jointly active. Ignition is a separate move, defined as going from a configuration holding a reserve to one with both sides active and the reserve used up; that it needs the reserve is the move's definition, and the reserve is present at the start, not formed by a promise. Promises force nothing (a separate witness, two events over the steps): "if the other eventually does, I eventually do" holds on both sides where neither ever happens. A witness, not a law of every circular dependence: that an actual joint activity meets the projections, the support or the one-step availability is not shown.

<a id="cooperation-read-as-giving-that-waits"></a>
### Cooperation read as giving that waits on giving

- **Mechanism.** An AI reading (D48), not a result. Cooperation among strangers is read as giving that waits on giving across chains longer than any acquaintance, and that more waiting gives no more as "the structural price of complexity". "Others will deceive me, so I deceive first" is read as withholding with memory, which absorbs. Kept promises and enforced contracts are read as laws giving first: the law changes, not the state alone. Tolerance is read as letting cooperation survive scattered withholding; where no formation spares all it waits on, it does not rebuild cooperation lost everywhere. Mutual eventual promises force nothing: "if the other eventually does, I eventually do" holds on both sides where neither ever happens. An exchange of harms is read as a loop: answering in kind keeps the difference, answering more runs away, so conflict institutions are links of another kind. A regulator is read as lagging wherever the world changes faster than it reads.
